ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 August 2019 on the operational implementation of the RBE; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012; amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended by laws introducing the Societe en Commandite Speciale (SCSp)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of non-expired passport of each ultimate beneficial owner and designated manager of the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or certified public document authority in the country of origin; if Luxembourg-issued, a Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incorporation of any corporate general partner or founding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home jurisdiction company registry, e.g., Companies House, Delaware Secretary of State, or equivalent competent authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank-issued proof of residential or business address for each UBO, dated less than three months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or utility provider in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney executed by all prospective partners appointing the Luxembourg formation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of signature

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds and banking relationship for each UBO contributing capital

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory application of Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004, CSSF Regulation 12-02 and EU AML Directives; every shareholder, UBO and intended manager must be screened against PEP classifications (foreign, national and domestic), OFAC SDN list and 50% ownership rule, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU Council consolidated financial sanctions and Luxembourg Finance Ministry blacklists; FATF high-risk jurisdiction flags require enhanced due diligence and additional source-of-wealth evidence; screening results must be archived in the formation and AML/CFT compliance file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS), official electronic portal at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Latin script; French, German or Luxembourgish transliteration is accepted; the SCSp must bear a distinctive and truthful name and must include the abbreviation 'S.C.Sp.' or the full phrase 'Societe en Commandite Speciale'; names must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing Luxembourg regulated or registered entity and must not contravene public order or mandatory legal form requirements.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon RCS name rejection, the applicant may file a written appeal with the Director of the Luxembourg Business Registers within one month from the date of notification; if the refusal is based on public policy or misleading-name grounds, the applicant may apply through counsel to the competent Minister of the Ministry of the Economy; further administrative recourse lies before the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within three months, supported by a legal memorandum and proposed amended name; parallel resubmission of a corrected name is permissible before or during the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for an SCSp engaged in non-regulated AI video synthesis or video-avatar SaaS licensing, provided that a recognised Luxembourg registered agent and a Luxembourg registered office address are maintained for formal service of process; a purely virtual address without local substance and without genuine management or decision-making presence in Luxembourg will not satisfy BEPS Action 5 transparency and substance expectations and may be challenged by tax authorities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, below 5% per annum for a non-regulated AIGC video SaaS business; RCS and tax authorities normally conduct desk-based audits, while unannounced physical on-site inspection may be triggered only by objective indicators of sham substance or tax abuse.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 concerning commercial companies (LCS), as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016 introducing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); Articles 1-58 (general partnership provisions as adapted) and the SCSp-specific provisions; RCS registration under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and the annual accounts of undertakings; electronic publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 11-13, boulevard de la Foire, L-1528 Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: RCS registration application filed electronically via the LBR e-filing portal (lbr.lu), comprising the constitutive act (partnership agreement) and statutory attachments, followed by mandatory publication in the RESA.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SCSp has no statutory minimum capital; partners freely determine the capital in the partnership agreement. Any agreed capital must be fully paid into a Luxembourg bank account or evidenced by a banker's certificate; in-kind contributions require a statutory auditor's report unless exempt. No escrow account is required under Luxembourg law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned General Partner of [SCSp name], acting under the Partnership Agreement and the Law of 10 August 1915, hereby: (1) approves the admission of the Limited Partner and the subscription to partnership interests as set out in Schedule A; (2) confirms the registered office at [address] in Luxembourg; (3) appoints [name] as sole manager with exclusive power to represent the SCSp; (4) authorises the manager to open bank accounts, file the RCS application, and appoint agents and representatives; (5) ratifies all preparatory expenses already incurred. This resolution takes effect immediately and remains in force until revoked by written consent of all partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name availability verification and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Trade and Companies Register (RCS) name search and reservation unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the RCS and LBR databases to confirm the proposed SCSp name is available and not misleading. File an electronic name reservation request via the LBR portal; the RCS issues a name availability confirmation, which remains valid for a limited period. The name should include or be accompanied by the words 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp'.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name and legal form identification
Identity documents of the general partner and limited partner(s)
Brief statement of the corporate purpose (ISIC 6201 – AI video synthesis and virtual avatar generation software)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to identity or confusion with an existing mark, request a reasoned decision from the RCS, correct or propose an alternative name, and refile without prejudice; no statutory cure fee is payable for rejection, but a new filing fee applies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the constitutive deed (partnership agreement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notarial Chamber of Luxembourg (Chambre des Notaires) for notarial execution, or private signature under the Law of 10 August 1915 if no real property contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement in accordance with LCS provisions for an SCSp: corporate name, legal form, registered office address, detailed corporate purpose (development, distribution and licensing of AI avatar video generation software and related SaaS services), unlimited duration, capital contributions, profit-sharing and distribution waterfall, management powers of the general partner, transfer restrictions, and voting rules. If contributions include immovable property, the deed must be executed before a Luxembourg notary; otherwise a written private deed is sufficient. Have all partners sign the deed and initial each schedule.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement (statuts)
RCS name availability confirmation
Passport or national ID of each partner
Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration forms
AML/KYC questionnaires and proof of source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS notifies a defect in the constitutive deed, correct the relevant clause by an amendatory act or notarial deed and resubmit the file; the correction is effective ex tunc where curative intent is evidenced.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a Luxembourg bank account and payment of agreed capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg banks (e.g., Banque Internationale à Luxembourg, Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Banque de Luxembourg) acting under CSSF AML/CFT supervision
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed constitutive deed and KYC documentation to the chosen bank and open an account in the name of the SCSp. Deposit the agreed cash capital contribution and obtain a banker's certificate (attestation bancaire) confirming the funds in the account. For in-kind contributions, obtain an independent valuation report or statutory auditor's certificate. This step is optional from a legal standpoint but strongly advisable for the RCS filing and the opening of payment rails (Stripe/Paddle).
required_dossiers: Executed constitutive deed (private or notarial)
Partners' identity documents and UBO declaration
Business plan and projected SaaS revenue model
Bank account opening forms and source-of-wealth documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional information under CSSF AML rules, provide enhanced due diligence documents; if the application is rejected, approach an alternative Luxembourg bank or request a reasoned refusal to support a complaint to the CSSF.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the incorporation file to the Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), electronic filing unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation package electronically through the LBR e-filing portal (lbr.lu) or via a notary. Include the constitutive deed, bank certificate or in-kind report, appointment of the general partner as manager, consent of the owner of the registered office premises, UBO declaration, and payment of the statutory registration fee. The RCS verifies legal compliance and issues the RCS registration number.
required_dossiers: Constitutive deed (private or notarial)
Banker's certificate of paid-in capital or auditor's report on in-kind contributions
Consent of the registered office holder (housing declaration)
Identity documents of managers and UBO declaration
Power of attorney where a representative files
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a defect notice (défaut de publicité), remedy the noted deficiencies within the statutory cure period, usually 15 days, and refile; engage the LBR helpdesk for technical errors and seek notarial correction where the act must be amended.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RESA publication and initial tax, VAT, and employer registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) for RESA publication; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT; Administration des Contributions Directes (Luxembourg tax administration) for corporate and municipal business tax registration; Joint Social Security Centre (CCSS) for employer registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, the RCS automatically publishes the constitutive documents in the RESA. Subsequently, file a VAT registration application via myguichet.lu within 15 days of the effective date of taxable supplies; apply for a Luxembourg VAT number; register for municipal business tax with the competent commune; file the declaration of commencement of activity with the direct tax administration; register as an employer with the CCSS if hiring staff.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract and registration number
Executed partnership agreement
Proof of registered office in Luxembourg
Declaration of commencement of activity (for direct tax administration)
VAT registration form (Formulaire 1) if turnover exceeds thresholds or for EU distance sales
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late VAT registration may attract penalties under the VAT law; file a voluntary disclosure with the AED, pay any security assessed, and register immediately; for CCSS late filings, submit a rectifying declaration and settle any minimal assessed contributions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Office premises certification and workplace compliance clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); communal fire safety authority (Service d'Incendie et de Secours); municipal building office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure a lease for the registered office in Luxembourg and obtain the landlord's fire safety and building compliance certificate for office occupancy. Conduct a workplace risk assessment, arrange emergency procedures, and register all employees with the CCSS prior to hiring. No industrial establishment permit is required for a pure software/SaaS activity, but the landlord's certificate of occupancy confirming fire safety and electrical conformity must be retained in the corporate file.
required_dossiers: Commercial lease agreement for the Luxembourg registered office
Fire safety compliance certificate for the premises
Workplace risk evaluation (Dossier d'évaluation des risques)
Electrical and building compliance attestation
Employee registration forms (IEM) with the CCSS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection identifies non-conformities, execute the remediation plan within the inspector's deadline and request a re-inspection; for structural concerns, obtain a licensed engineer's assessment and submit a corrective report to the commune.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy, General Directorate for Industry and Innovation (Ministère de l'Économie) – referenced only as the supervisory authority; no industrial establishment permit applies to ISIC 6201 (software publication/AI SaaS).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating or manufacturing permit is required for the AI avatar video generation software activity. The activity is not a regulated activities list item under Luxembourg law and is subject only to general e-commerce rules (Law of 28 May 2019 on e-commerce) and data protection requirements (GDPR).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not classified – the pure digital service activity does not fall within the annex of the amended Law of 15 June 2018 on environmental impact assessment; no EIA report, environmental consent or registration required for the AI SaaS software operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for a zero-discharge software activity. If an on-premises data centre or high-density server room is later installed, the operator must comply with EU F-Gas Regulation 517/2014 regarding cooling equipment, the amended Law of 19 December 2008 on water management for any wastewater from cooling, and the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste management for e-waste; no VOC or industrial discharge thresholds trigger.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office occupancy requires a fire safety certification issued by the communal fire inspection service; structural load inspections are only relevant if heavy server racks are installed and must be certified by a Luxembourg-licensed engineer; occupational clearance requires an ITM workplace risk assessment and CCSS employee registration before any hiring, but no special civil defense licence is imposed for administrative software development premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) for RCS company registration; digital portals: MyGuichet.lu, lbr.lu, aedt.public.lu, and tax.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) File the SCSp partnership agreement with the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) through the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) platform to obtain the 15-digit national business number (matricule); 2) Register for VAT with the AEDT via MyGuichet using the matricule, obtaining an LU + 8-digit VAT number; 3) For direct tax, the fiscally transparent SCSp is not separately registered for CIT — each partner is assessed under its own residence tax number; non-resident partners file Luxembourg income tax declarations through a Luxembourg tax representative where required; 4) A non-EU-resident SCSp or foreign partner making taxable Luxembourg supplies must appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative before AEDT registration, whereas EU-resident entities register directly; 5) Confirm municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) obligations with the competent commune, which may apply at the SCSp level despite income tax transparency.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Luxembourg; the SCSp is mandatorily fiscally transparent for income tax (partners taxed in their own hands). For VAT, the SCSp is treated as an independent taxable person and may be required to register upon making taxable supplies. Anti-hybrid rules (ATAD) override transparency where cross-border hybrid arrangements create double non-taxation or deduction/non-inclusion mismatches. The partnership may structure contractual profit-allocation (targeted allocations, tracking or sub-accounts) to shape partner-level taxable income, but cannot elect entity-level CIT liability.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA) under the Luxembourg VAT Act (loi TVA), transposing EU Directive 2006/112/EC, complemented by the VAT OSS/IOSS regimes
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover small-business exemption for locally established taxable persons; for non-established e-commerce suppliers of digitally supplied services (B2C) the intra-EU distance-sales/OSS registration threshold is EUR 10,000 per calendar year; B2B services to Luxembourg businesses are not registrable by the supplier because the reverse charge shifts VAT to the Luxembourg customer; non-EU suppliers may opt for the Union OSS to avoid local VAT registration for remote B2C supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory digital stamping, or continuous transaction controls currently apply in Luxembourg. E-invoicing is compulsory only for suppliers to Luxembourg public contracting authorities (B2G) in Peppol/EN16931 format; B2B e-invoicing remains optional. Luxembourg will implement the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) digital reporting obligations from 2028/2030; all invoices, e-invoices and export documentation must be retained for 6 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to qualifying exports of goods to destinations outside the EU where the goods physically leave the EU within 90 days and transport is evidenced. The AI avatar video generation software and associated SaaS services are electronically supplied services: B2B supplies to non-EU customers are outside Luxembourg VAT (place of supply at customer's establishment); B2C supplies to non-EU consumers are outside scope (place of supply at consumer's residence); B2B supplies to EU customers are reverse-charged; only B2C supplies to Luxembourg consumers attract Luxembourg VAT at 17%. Export-related services directly linked to exported goods may also qualify for 0% under the VAT Act subject to strict documentary proof.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Single Administrative Document (e-SAD) customs export declaration accepted by Luxembourg customs
Bill of lading, air waybill, or CMR transport document evidencing physical exit from the EU
Commercial invoice, export contract and purchase order
Destination-country customs clearance or import entry documentation (where available)
Bank payment evidence or foreign inward remittance records supporting transaction genuineness
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT and Luxembourg customs conduct post-clearance audits of zero-rated and outside-scope exports; defective documentation triggers reassessment at 17% VAT, statutory default interest, and administrative fines (up to 10% of the evaded tax for negligence and up to double the evaded tax for intentional fraud). Criminal tax fraud (fraude fiscale) is punishable by imprisonment (up to 5 years) and significant fines; the re-assessment limitation period is extended in cases of fraud; because the SCSp is fiscally transparent, direct partners remain jointly liable for any tax clawback in proportion to their profit split.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area state with full current and capital account convertibility. The free movement of capital is guaranteed under Articles 63-65 TFEU and Luxembourg implements no general exchange controls or currency equalization restrictions. A Luxembourg Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) is fiscally transparent, and profit remittances to foreign partners are not subject to Luxembourg domestic withholding tax at the level of the partnership; all distributions are paid gross, though the tax treatment of the partner depends on the partner's own residence and the applicable double tax treaty framework. No administrative authorization is required for remittance, subject to normal AML/CFT and CRS/FATCA reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender rule or mandatory conversion ratio exists in Luxembourg. Exporters of software/SaaS services and AI-generated content may retain and freely use foreign currency proceeds without any forced conversion into euro or any BCL reporting deadline. Only standard statistical balance-of-payments reporting thresholds and AML transaction reporting requirements apply, and they do not restrict the timing or convertibility of export receipts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Multi-Currency Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High (conditional). An EU/EEA licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) may operate as a supplementary collection and payment rail for the SaaS revenue, but it is not a substitute for a regulated credit institution for escrow or capital-commitment purposes. Legal constraints: the SCSp must be the named account holder; e-money safeguarding rules under the Electronic Money Directive (2009/110/EC) apply; the EMI cannot provide lending or escrow-grade settlement; and the bank/non-bank relationship is subject to strict AML/KYC and PM-L/CFT compliance at both the EMI and the underlying payment processor (Stripe/Paddle) level.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of the authorised managers or general partner representatives is generally required during onboarding at Luxembourg commercial banks. Remote or video-KYC account opening is rarely available for a pass-through partnership with non-resident ultimate beneficial owners; a physical meeting in Luxembourg is the default mandate to avoid refusal or prolonged compliance review. Bank compliance may also ask for an in-person interview to verify the business model, the identity of the AI avatar video-generation activity, and the source of wealth/capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity of the SCSp and non-resident partnership investors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and filed SCSp partnership agreement; RCS/Luxembourg Business Registers certificate; up-to-date UBO declaration filed in the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE); capital call letters and subscription agreements; audited or accountant-verified financial statements; detailed source-of-funds evidence for each investor, including bank statements and tax status documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border AI SaaS revenue routing through Stripe/Paddle and possible digital-asset-adjacent proceeds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execution copies of Stripe/Paddle merchant agreements and payout schedules; consolidated revenue summaries linked to bank statements; end-client invoices and order/transaction records; clear description of the AI video synthesis and virtual avatar software business; GDPR and data-protection compliance documentation; model governance and IP ownership evidence; confirmation that no cryptocurrency or money-service-business activity is present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FATCA/CRS classification uncertainty for the foreign-owned transparent partnership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg tax opinion confirming pass-through classification; CRS and FATCA self-certification of all partners; Luxembourg registrations for FATCA/CRS; permanent establishment analysis; historical tax reporting from previous financial years; representation letter to the bank on non-financial-entity (NFE) versus financial-institution status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reputational and financial-crime risk in AI-generated content and virtual avatar monetisation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IP assignments and trademark/patent registrations; model content moderation and acceptable-use policy; commercial contracts confirming lawful end-use; ISO 27001 or SOC 2 attestation if available; AML risk self-assessment demonstrating a low-risk standard banking tier; corporate rollout plan and business jurisdiction analysis.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing requires the use of SWIFT MT103 (or equivalent ISO 20022 payment) from the investor's own bank account to the SCSp's IBAN at its Luxembourg commercial bank, with a reference clearly stating 'Capital Contribution to LU SCSp' or 'Equity Subscription'. The payment must be accompanied by a capital contribution deed, notarized partnership documentation, and an updated share/sedimentation register. The receiving bank performs beneficiary and source-of-funds checks; amounts above EUR 10,000 may require standard AML verification and, if triggered, enhanced due diligence. The purpose code can be referenced as 'Direct Investment' under the BPM6 balance-of-payments classification; BCL statistical reporting obligations rest on the bank rather than the SCSp.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail for non-EEA trade settlements is SWIFT MT103/MT202 for international wire transfers, with the beneficiary account name, IBAN/SWIFT BIC, and a regulatory reference of 'Trade Settlement' or 'Service Fee'. For intra-EEA euro-denominated disbursements, SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT) are the standard low-cost rail. For goods or intellectual-property acquisition with documentary risk, a documentary commercial letter of credit (SWIFT MT700), followed by amendment via MT707 and honour under UCP600, is available through the Luxembourg commercial bank. Multi-currency disbursements are settled through nostro/vostro accounts and do not require CSSF or BCL pre-approval.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD FX forwards executed with EU/EEA regulated banks or investment firms
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where the settlement currency is non-convertible or restricted by the counterparty jurisdiction
Cross-currency swaps (EUR versus USD, GBP, JPY or other freely convertible currencies) for long-term liquidity and certainty
FX options and currency collars for board-approved treasury risk management, subject to EMIR clearing, reporting and margining obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RCS Annual Confirmation (confirmation annuelle) — Article 15 of the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS and LBR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed annually within one month following the RCS registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers administrative fines up to EUR 500; repeated failure after formal notice may result in administrative strike-off from the RCS, loss of the active registration file, and inability to obtain official extracts or certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO information update and re-confirmation in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No standalone annual UBO declaration; data must be re-confirmed through the RCS Annual Confirmation and updated within one month after each change in partnership interests or beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or incorrect UBO disclosure exposes the SCSp, its managers, and partners to administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 per breach and, in serious cases, criminal sanctions under the amended Law of 13 January 2019.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and statutory audit file (where applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) for publication when applicable; CSSF for regulated SCSp vehicles
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 8 months after the financial year-end if filing or publication is applicable; accounting records must be closed annually and kept available for partners.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A non-regulated SCSp is not subject to public annual accounts filing; if the SCSp is an Alternative Investment Fund or Part II UCI, late filing triggers CSSF enforcement measures, administrative fines, and possible suspension of the vehicle.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No direct capital or size-based audit threshold for an SCSp because it lacks legal personality; a mandatory audit arises only if the SCSp is an Alternative Investment Fund under the AIFM Law, a Part II UCI, a regulated fund vehicle, or if the limited partnership agreement expressly requires an independent audit by an approved Luxembourg statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under Book III of the Luxembourg Commercial Code; IFRS permitted on a voluntary basis and required for certain regulated or consolidated reporting entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The RBE record, accessible through LBR, must at all times identify the natural-person beneficial owners. For an SCSp, any transfer of partnership interests must be documented and notified to the RBE within one month. The RCS Annual Confirmation serves as the annual re-confirmation of UBO data; partners and the general partner should sign a year-end beneficial-ownership confirmation before the filing. The registered agent should also perform an annual internal register audit against the limited partnership agreement and the RCS/RBE records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners / Members (Registre des Associés)
Register of General Partners and Managers (Directors-equivalent)
Minute Book of Partner and Manager Resolutions
UBO Register Extract / RBE Documentation File maintained at the registered office

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if no statutory audit; if required, USD 8,000–20,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Luxembourg corporate income tax headline rate of 17% for fiscal year 2024; for corporate partners of an SCSp the aggregate rate in Luxembourg City including solidarity surcharge (7% of CIT) and communal business tax (6.75%) is 24.94%. The SCSp itself, being fiscally transparent (pass-through), is not subject to CIT at the entity level; its profits are allocated to partners who are taxed at their own applicable rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption for qualifying dividend and capital gain income (min. 10% shareholding held for 12 months, or EUR 1.2 million acquisition price); IP box regime providing a 50% deduction on net income derived from qualifying IP assets; no net wealth tax for SCSp (though corporate partners may be subject to net wealth tax); parent-subsidiary directive provides 0% withholding on qualifying dividends; Luxembourg tax ruling practice permits upfront certainty on SPV structures.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward for Luxembourg corporate income tax losses; however, annual offset of carried-forward losses is limited to 17% of positive taxable income exceeding EUR 17,402,806 (2024 threshold). For SCSp, losses pass through to partners and are deductible in accordance with the partners' own regimes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Luxembourg partnership income tax return (personnes morales non-collectivement imposables) — Form 160; electronic filing via MyGuichet.lu / ACD e-filing portal (LuxTrust authentication).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Standard deadline: 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end (e.g., for FY ending 31 Dec 2024, due 31 Dec 2025). If the fiscal year ends on a different date, the return is due on the last day of the 12th month following the fiscal year-end. AUDIT: e-filing grants an automatic extension to 30 June of the second year following the fiscal year-end, provided no tax due remains outstanding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RCS number, VAT number, national registration number, registered office address, principal business activity code (NACE/ISIC 6201), legal form code for SCSp.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners need only provide their own identification and tax residence certificate if claiming treaty relief; the SCSp itself must be fully identified in the Luxembourg RCS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates; accounting framework (Luxembourg GAAP / IFRS); indication whether the return is the initial return, amendment, or liquidation return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must cause the SCSp to present accurate calendar year figures if the SCSp uses a different fiscal year; the SCSp's fiscal year is determined by the partnership agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit or loss as computed for Luxembourg tax purposes, after add-backs and deductions under the LIR; includes all revenues from AI video synthesis and virtual avatar subscriptions, licensing, one-off service fees, and other commercial income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Income must be allocated to each partner according to his economic interest in the SCSp. Non-resident partners are taxable in Luxembourg to the extent the income is attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment; otherwise, the income is outside Luxembourg tax scope (unless Luxembourg real estate or certain Luxembourg source income).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List of each partner: full name / company name, address, Luxembourg tax number (if any), participation percentage, profit share, loss share, and any special allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, provide a certificate of tax residence (TRC) for the relevant fiscal year; if the SCSp has made a check-the-box election to be treated as transparent, no additional filing is required at the SCSp level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All eligible deductions: IP box net deduction, investment tax credit, notional interest deduction (for new equity financing), participation exemption claims, and foreign tax credits on underlying income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners cannot directly claim Luxembourg personal or corporate tax credits through the SCSp; the SCSp return is informational only. Partners must apply credits on their own returns.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: fixed EUR 250 to EUR 5,000, plus an automatic penalty of 0.5% of the tax due per month, capped at 15% of the total tax; late payment interest accrues at 0.8% per month; criminal penalties for intentional non-filing include fines up to EUR 500,000 and/or imprisonment of the responsible manager in severe cases.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for payments by an SCSp to its partners, as the SCSp is fiscally transparent and distributions of profits are not regarded as dividends; they represent additional remuneration or returns of capital. If the SCSp were subject to an election to be treated as a taxable corporation, the standard Luxembourg dividend withholding tax rate would be 15%, reduced to 0% under the parent-subsidiary regime (≥10% shareholding, 12-month holding) or 5% under certain tax treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Since no withholding is imposed on SCSp profit distributions, treaty relief is generally not required for the distribution itself. For any withholding arising on other Luxembourg-sourced payments (e.g., deemed interest, royalties), the beneficial owner must file an application with the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes) using the standard Certificate of Tax Residence (Form 900) and a completed withholding tax exemption attestation. The application must be submitted prior to or at the payment date; the payer will then apply the reduced rate at source. For Belgium, France, Germany and other treaty partners with an SCSp, partners must provide their own TRC and a statement of effective beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose withholding tax on outbound interest or royalty payments (excluding certain interest that is profit-linked). The statutory rate is 0% for both interest and royalties. In case of a double tax treaty, the treaty rate is also typically 0% (Luxembourg has not ratified royalty articles that deviate; however, some agreements restrict the 0% deduction). The absence of WHT is subject to the beneficial ownership requirement and transparancy rules under the Luxembourg GAAR.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg adheres to the OECD TP Documentation Guidelines and EU Transfer Pricing Directives. Mandatory preparation of a Master File and Local File for the Luxembourg entity if: (1) the international group's consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 50 million; and (2) the Luxembourg entity's controlled transactions exceed EUR 100,000 per category (financing, intangibles, services) in a fiscal period. The local file must be filed electronically with the Luxembourg tax administration within 12 months after the fiscal year-end (but must be available immediately upon request during an audit).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply the UK-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the law requires a certain level of economic substance to obtain and maintain tax residency, to benefit from the IP box regime, and to invoke tax treaty protection. The Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority's Circular L.I.R. n° 14/4 on tax residency requires offices, staff, and decision-making functions in Luxembourg. The ATAD (EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive) including the GAAR (General Anti-Abuse Rule) will disregard artificial structures lacking substance. For an SCSp generating AI video software income, the entity must demonstrate real business activity, such as the presence of contractual personnel, license management, and management of development risks. Failure to meet substance requirements can lead to recharacterization of the structure and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating AI video synthesis revenue, overstating royalties or service payments to related companies, deliberately omitting intercompany licenses, or filing false documentation in the SCSp tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed fine of EUR 5,000 to EUR 50,000 plus a late payment interest of 0.8% per month; if tax evasion is established, the tax administration may reassess income for up to 10 years; the amount of evaded tax is due together with an administrative penalty of 10% of the evaded tax, which can rise to 50% in case of a repeated offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Luxembourg law allows the tax administration to pierce the corporate veil where the SCSp has been used fraudulently. Directors may be jointly and severally liable for corpores tax debts if they have knowingly signed false statements. Criminal penalties include imprisonment from 1 to 5 years and fines up to EUR 500,000. Travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed during the criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Company / Lack of Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp without any physical presence, employees, bank account, or real decision-making in Luxembourg; the SCSp serves solely as a conduit to route AI avatar platform revenues to a low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Luxembourg tax administration can disregard the SCSp for tax purposes (substance over form), deny the applicable treaty or EU directive benefits, and assess tax on the deemed Luxembourg resident beneficiary. Administrative penalties up to EUR 10,000 may be imposed for filing incomplete or false statements on economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell SCSp may be held personally liable for taxes due, interest, and penalties if they are deemed to have exercised actual control over the entity's operations. On sham company findings, directors may face civil liability for the total loss suffered by the tax authority, and the criminal sanction includes disqualification from managing a Luxembourg entity and a custodial sentence up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The AI video generation platform processes payments from end-users; the SCSp fails to maintain a Luxembourg beneficial ownership register (RBE) or files incomplete information; monies derived from global software sales are laundered through the SCSp to hide tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004 (AML) and PPPA 2023, failure to register beneficial ownership results in a fine of EUR 1,000 to EUR 20,000 per month of non-compliance. AML violations trigger administrative penalties from EUR 20,000 to EUR 1,000,000; criminal money laundering sanctions include imprisonment from 5 to 10 years and fines up to EUR 1,250,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors (including managers of an SCSp who direct the platform) are personally liable for AML breaches if they knowingly neglect their duty to report suspicious transactions. They may receive EU-wide asset freezing orders, travel prohibitions, and imprisonment up to 8 years for money laundering facilitation. The Luxembourg financial regulator (CSSF) will ban the individual from holding compliance or management positions in regulated entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging excessive management fees, royalty payments, or deployment fees to the AI avatar video generation entity without an arm's length analysis; creating intercompany financing with non-economic yields to shift profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable profits to the arm's length standard, assessment of additional CIT, municipal business tax, and solidarity surcharge (aggregate rate up to 24.94%). A penalty of up to 50% of the extra tax may be imposed if the pricing is not supported by contemporaneous benchmarking; late interest applies retrospectively.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If directors permit a deliberate, undocumented transfer pricing scheme, the Luxembourg tax administration may assert personal liability for the additional tax and penalties. In case of fraudulent mispricing, criminal proceedings for tax evasion could lead to imprisonment of the responsible finance director.
